newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Volatility trades established in FTSE.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Volatility trades established in FTSE.

text.p: Volatility trades in FTSE 100 index options were the main deals in UK equity options on Thursday as the stock market wobbled then flattened out, dealers said.

One such deal was to buy 1,000 June 4225 calls at 48-1/2p against selling June FTSE futures at 4700. If properly hedged the gains/losses from the long calls as the market moves higher/lower will be offset by losses/gains from the short futures position.
The deal will make a profit if market volatility increases up to June expiry.
Other, more complex deals, involved hedging a futures position against a spread trade with FTSE options and some traders rolled foward near-term positions to a longer-dated expiry month.

One of the larger trades in the latter category was to buy back 500 June 4775 calls at 25p and to sell 500 July 4825 calls at 41p hoping to capture option premium if the market stays below 4825 by July expiry.
By 1447 GMT, cash FTSE was up 0.9 at 4678.4 while June futures were up 1.0 at 4689.0.
In stock options, Lloyds TSB Group was active from a crossed trade in which 1,250 December 700 calls were traded at 37p. The banking group's shares fell 10p to 629p.

Elsewhere, a long straddle was the main deal in conglomerate BTR in which 350 November 200 puts and calls were bought at 16p and 17p each. The deal will be profitable if the underlying shares become volatile and move as far as possible away from the strike price. BTR shares shed 9p to 197p.
